questions.q: Which of the following is a liquid at room temperature?
questions.explanation: Mercury is the metal that is liquid at ordinary room temperature.

questions.q: Which of the following is not matter?
questions.explanation: Matter has mass and occupies space; light is a form of energy and has neither.

questions.q: The temperature at which a liquid starts boiling at atmospheric pressure is its
questions.explanation: This temperature is called the boiling point.

questions.q: Which order shows the space between particles from least to most?
questions.explanation: Particles are closest in a solid and farthest apart in a gas.

questions.q: Which of the following would decrease the rate of evaporation of a liquid?
options: Increasing the humidity of the air
questions.explanation: Air that already holds a lot of water vapour takes up less vapour from the liquid.

questions.q: A desert cooler works better on a dry day than on a humid day because
options: the day is hotter when it is dry
evaporation of water is faster when the air has low humidity
the water in the cooler is colder on dry days
the fan runs faster on dry days
questions.explanation: Faster evaporation of water removes more heat and gives more cooling.

questions.q: When ice at 0 °C changes to water at 0 °C, which statement is correct?
options: The particles gain energy and move more freely
There is no change in the energy of the particles
questions.explanation: Heat absorbed during melting increases the energy of the particles, so they can move more freely.

questions.q: Convert 25 °C to kelvin and 300 K to degrees Celsius.
questions.explanation: The kelvin scale starts at 273 below the Celsius zero (rounded).

questions.q: Why does water in an earthen pot (matka) become cool in summer?
questions.answer: The earthen pot has very tiny pores through which water seeps to the outer surface and evaporates. The evaporation takes heat from the water in the pot, so the water becomes cool.
keyPoints: Evaporation takes heat from the water inside
questions.explanation: Evaporation causes cooling.

questions.q: Which of the following is a heterogeneous mixture?
questions.explanation: In sand and water the two components are visible and not uniformly mixed.

questions.q: The component of a solution that dissolves the solute is called the
questions.explanation: The solvent is the substance that dissolves the solute.

questions.q: Elements can be broadly classified as
questions.explanation: Elements are grouped by properties into metals, non-metals and metalloids.

questions.q: Which of the following is a metalloid?
questions.explanation: Silicon shows properties of both metals and non-metals.

questions.q: Which non-metal is a liquid at room temperature?
questions.explanation: Bromine is the only non-metal that is liquid at room temperature.

questions.q: Which of the following is a colloid?
questions.explanation: Fog has tiny water droplets dispersed in air, which is a colloid.

questions.q: Chalk powder is stirred into water. The mixture looks milky but the chalk settles slowly on standing. The mixture is a
questions.explanation: Particles that settle on standing form a suspension.

questions.q: Give two differences between a true solution and a suspension.
questions.answer: In a true solution the particles are very small, do not settle and pass through filter paper, and the solution is transparent. In a suspension the particles are large, settle on standing, can be filtered out and the mixture is opaque or cloudy.
keyPoints: Particles of true solution are tiny
Suspension can be filtered, solution cannot
questions.explanation: The difference lies mainly in particle size.

questions.q: How will you separate (a) a mixture of kerosene oil and water and (b) a mixture of ethanol and water?
questions.answer: (a) Kerosene and water are immiscible, so they are separated by a separating funnel, where the lower layer is run off. (b) Ethanol and water are miscible but have different boiling points, so they are separated by fractional distillation, in which the ethanol, which boils first, is collected.
keyPoints: Miscible liquids with different boiling points use distillation
questions.explanation: The method is chosen from the property that differs between the liquids.

questions.q: The law of constant proportions was stated by
questions.explanation: Proust stated that a compound always contains the same elements in a fixed ratio by mass.

questions.q: The chemical symbol of gold is
questions.explanation: Au comes from the Latin name aurum.

questions.q: The chemical symbol of silver is
questions.explanation: Ag comes from the Latin name argentum.

questions.q: The molecular mass of hydrogen chloride, HCl, is (H = 1 u, Cl = 35.5 u)
The number of molecules in 2 moles of a substance is
Which of the following chemical formulae is written correctly?
questions.explanation: Potassium has valency 1 and oxygen has valency 2, so the formula is K2O.

questions.q: What is the mass of 0.5 mole of carbon dioxide? (C = 12 u, O = 16 u)
State any two postulates of Dalton's atomic theory.
questions.answer: All matter is made of very small particles called atoms, which cannot be divided or created or destroyed in a chemical reaction. Atoms of the same element are identical in mass and properties, while atoms of different elements have different masses and properties.
questions.explanation: Later discoveries showed that atoms can be divided into subatomic particles and that isotopes exist.

questions.q: Find the number of atoms in 0.1 mole of water, H2O. (Avogadro constant = 6.022 × 10^23)
questions.answer: Number of molecules = 0.1 × 6.022 × 10^23 = 6.022 × 10^22. Each molecule has 3 atoms, so the number of atoms = 3 × 6.022 × 10^22 = 1.8066 × 10^23.
questions.explanation: Multiply the number of molecules by the atoms per molecule.

questions.q: The neutron was discovered by
questions.explanation: Chadwick discovered the neutron in 1932.

questions.q: An atom has 6 protons and 6 neutrons. Its mass number is
questions.explanation: Mass number = 6 + 6 = 12.

questions.q: The number of electrons in the outermost shell of a sodium atom (2, 8, 1) is
questions.explanation: The outermost shell of sodium has one electron.

questions.q: The isotopes of hydrogen (protium, deuterium and tritium) differ in their
questions.explanation: They all have one proton but 0, 1 and 2 neutrons respectively.

questions.q: The valency of neon (electronic configuration 2, 8) is
questions.explanation: Its outer shell is complete, so it neither gains nor loses electrons.

questions.q: A chloride ion, Cl−, has how many electrons? (atomic number of chlorine = 17)
questions.explanation: The atom has 17 electrons, and the ion has gained one, giving 18.

questions.q: Which of the following has 10 electrons? (atomic numbers: Na = 11, Mg = 12, Cl = 17, F = 9)
questions.explanation: F has 9 electrons and F− has gained one, giving 10.

questions.q: State two postulates of Bohr's model of the atom.
questions.answer: Electrons revolve around the nucleus only in certain special orbits (shells) called discrete orbits. While an electron stays in one of these orbits it does not radiate energy.
keyPoints: No energy is radiated in these orbits
questions.explanation: This explained why the atom is stable.

questions.q: Explain how sodium and chlorine atoms each acquire a stable electronic arrangement when they form sodium chloride.
questions.answer: A sodium atom (2, 8, 1) loses one electron to become Na+ (2, 8), and a chlorine atom (2, 8, 7) gains that electron to become Cl− (2, 8, 8). Both then have complete outer shells, and the oppositely charged ions attract each other to form NaCl.
keyPoints: Both get a complete outer shell
questions.explanation: Atoms combine to reach the stable octet.

questions.q: Who was the first to describe free-living cells such as bacteria and protozoa?
questions.explanation: Leeuwenhoek first saw living cells using his own microscope.

questions.q: Chromosomes are made up of
questions.explanation: Chromosomes in the nucleus are made of DNA and proteins.

questions.q: Which of the following is a prokaryotic cell?
questions.explanation: Bacteria have no membrane-bound nucleus.

questions.q: Chromoplasts are plastids that contain
questions.explanation: Chromoplasts give colours such as yellow, orange and red to flowers and fruits.

questions.q: Colourless plastids that store starch, oils and proteins are called
questions.explanation: Leucoplasts are the storage plastids.

questions.q: The plasma membrane is said to be selectively permeable because it
options: allows some substances to pass through but not others
questions.explanation: It controls the entry and exit of materials.

questions.q: A dry raisin swells when placed in water. This is because
options: water enters the raisin by osmosis since the water concentration is lower inside it
questions.explanation: Water moves from a higher to a lower water concentration through the raisin's membrane.

questions.q: What are chromosomes? State their role.
questions.answer: Chromosomes are thread-like structures in the nucleus, made of DNA and proteins, which become visible when the cell divides. They carry the genes and pass on characters from parents to offspring.
questions.explanation: Chromosomes are the carriers of heredity.

questions.q: Under a microscope a student sees a cell with a cell wall, a large central vacuole and chloroplasts. Identify the type of cell and give two reasons.
questions.answer: It is a plant cell. Cell walls and chloroplasts occur only in plant cells and not in animal cells, and a large central vacuole is also a typical feature of plant cells.
questions.explanation: These features separate plant cells from animal cells.

questions.q: The fluid connective tissue that carries oxygen and nutrients around the body is
questions.explanation: Blood transports oxygen, food and wastes.

questions.q: The hard matrix of bone is rich in
questions.explanation: Calcium and phosphorus compounds make bone hard.

questions.q: The outermost protective layer of the parts of a plant is the
questions.explanation: The epidermis covers and protects the plant parts.

questions.q: The stomata in the epidermis of a leaf help in
questions.explanation: Stomata allow exchange of gases and loss of water vapour.

questions.q: Which simple permanent tissue has thin-walled, loosely packed living cells that store food?
questions.explanation: Parenchyma cells are thin-walled and often store food.

questions.q: Which statement about smooth muscle is correct?
options: Its cells are spindle-shaped with a single nucleus
Its cells are striped with many nuclei
It is found in the limbs
questions.explanation: Smooth muscle cells are spindle-shaped, unstriped and involuntary, as in the intestine.

questions.q: A ring of bark is removed all around the stem of a tree. The movement of food from the leaves to the roots stops because the
questions.explanation: Phloem lies in the bark and carries food from leaves to other parts.

questions.q: State two features of meristematic tissue.
questions.answer: Meristematic tissue consists of actively dividing cells. Its cells are thin-walled, closely packed with dense cytoplasm and a prominent nucleus, and they have little or no vacuole.
questions.explanation: These features suit the job of making new cells.

questions.q: How do plants increase in length and in thickness? Name the tissues responsible.
questions.answer: Plants grow in length because of the apical meristem at the tips of roots and shoots. They grow in thickness because of the lateral meristem (cambium) present along the sides of stems and roots.
keyPoints: Thickness by lateral meristem or cambium
questions.explanation: Each growth direction depends on a different meristem.

questions.q: The SI unit of acceleration is
questions.explanation: Acceleration is change in velocity per second, in m/s².

questions.q: A body moving in a straight line with uniform velocity has an acceleration that is
questions.explanation: If velocity does not change, the acceleration is zero.

questions.q: The speedometer of a car shows
questions.explanation: A speedometer reads the speed at the moment of observation.

questions.q: A body moves 100 m in 10 s and then 50 m in the next 5 s along a straight line. Its average speed is
questions.explanation: Total distance 150 m in 15 s gives 10 m/s.

questions.q: A car has an initial velocity of 5 m/s and a uniform acceleration of 3 m/s². Its velocity after 4 s is
A ball dropped from the top of a tower takes 3 s to reach the ground. The height of the tower is (g = 9.8 m/s²)
A horizontal straight line above the time axis in a velocity-time graph shows that the body has
questions.explanation: The velocity is constant, so there is no acceleration.

questions.q: Distinguish between speed and velocity.
questions.answer: Speed is the distance travelled per unit time and is a scalar with magnitude only. Velocity is the displacement per unit time in a given direction and is a vector with both magnitude and direction.
questions.explanation: Speed does not tell the direction; velocity does.

questions.q: A body accelerates uniformly from rest to 10 m/s in 5 s and then moves at 10 m/s for another 5 s. Find the total distance covered using the velocity-time graph.
questions.answer: In the first 5 s the area under the graph is a triangle: ½ × 5 × 10 = 25 m. In the next 5 s the area is a rectangle: 10 × 5 = 50 m. Total distance = 75 m.
questions.explanation: The area under a velocity-time graph gives the distance covered.

questions.q: A force can change
options: only the shape of a body
the speed, direction of motion or shape of a body
only the colour of a body
questions.explanation: A force can start or stop motion, change speed or direction, or change shape.

questions.q: One newton is equal to
questions.explanation: 1 N = 1 kg × 1 m/s².

questions.q: Dust comes out of a carpet when it is beaten with a stick because
options: the carpet moves but the dust particles tend to remain at rest
questions.explanation: This is inertia of rest: the dust stays in place as the carpet moves.

questions.q: A force of 20 N acts on a 4 kg body. Its acceleration is
A 0.5 kg ball hits a wall at 4 m/s and rebounds at 4 m/s. The change in its momentum is
A truck collides head-on with a small car. The force that the truck exerts on the car, compared with the force the car exerts on the truck, is
questions.explanation: By Newton's third law the two forces are equal and opposite.

questions.q: A 10 g bullet moving at 400 m/s embeds in a wooden block and stops in 0.01 s. The average force on the bullet is
questions.explanation: Change in momentum = 0.01 × 400 = 4 kg m/s, so F = 4 / 0.01 = 400 N.

questions.q: Differentiate between balanced and unbalanced forces.
questions.answer: Balanced forces are forces that cancel each other so that the net force is zero and the state of motion does not change. Unbalanced forces have a non-zero net force, which changes the speed or direction of motion of the body.
keyPoints: Balanced: net force zero, no change in motion
Unbalanced: net force non-zero, motion changes
questions.explanation: Only an unbalanced force produces acceleration.

questions.q: Why does a loaded truck need a larger force to stop in the same time than an empty truck moving at the same speed?
questions.answer: The loaded truck has a greater mass, so at the same speed it has a greater momentum. To change this momentum to zero in the same time needs a greater force, since force equals the rate of change of momentum.
questions.explanation: Greater momentum means a greater force for the same stopping time.

questions.q: The SI unit of density is
questions.explanation: Density is mass per unit volume.

questions.q: The statement that the upthrust on a body immersed in a fluid equals the weight of the fluid it displaces is
questions.explanation: This is Archimedes' principle.

questions.q: An object has a mass of 500 g and a volume of 250 cm³. Its density is
questions.explanation: Density = 500 / 250 = 2 g/cm³.

questions.q: An object weighs 50 N in air and 30 N when completely immersed in water. The buoyant force on it is
questions.explanation: Buoyant force = loss of apparent weight = 50 − 30 = 20 N.

questions.q: We feel lighter when we are in water because
options: water exerts an upward buoyant force on us
questions.explanation: The upthrust of water partly balances our weight.

questions.q: At a distance from the Earth's centre equal to twice the Earth's radius, the acceleration due to gravity is (g = value at the surface)
questions.explanation: g varies inversely as the square of the distance, so doubling the distance divides g by four.

questions.q: What is free fall? What is the acceleration of a freely falling body near the Earth?
questions.answer: Free fall is the motion of a body falling towards the Earth under the force of gravity alone, with no air resistance. Its acceleration is about 9.8 m/s² for all bodies.
questions.explanation: The acceleration due to gravity does not depend on the mass of the body.

questions.q: A stone of mass 2 kg is dropped from a height of 20 m. Find its velocity just before it hits the ground. (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.answer: Using v² = u² + 2gh with u = 0: v² = 2 × 10 × 20 = 400, so v = 20 m/s.
questions.explanation: The mass of the stone does not affect its speed in free fall.

questions.q: Work done by a force is positive when the force and the displacement are
questions.explanation: A force along the displacement does positive work.

questions.q: The commercial unit of electrical energy is the
questions.explanation: Electricity bills are in units of kilowatt-hours.

questions.q: One watt is equal to
questions.explanation: Power is the rate of doing work; 1 W = 1 J/s.

questions.q: A force of 15 N moves an object 4 m in the direction of the force. The work done is
The energy of the Sun comes mainly from
questions.explanation: In the Sun, hydrogen nuclei fuse to form helium and release energy.

questions.q: A 2 kg ball is dropped from a height of 10 m. Its kinetic energy just before hitting the ground is (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: KE equals the loss of potential energy: mgh = 2 × 10 × 10 = 200 J.

questions.q: What is power? State its SI unit.
questions.answer: Power is the rate of doing work, or the work done per unit time (P = W / t). Its SI unit is the watt (W), and 1 W = 1 J/s.
questions.explanation: A machine that does the same work faster has more power.

questions.q: A pump raises 100 kg of water to a height of 10 m in 20 s. Find the power of the pump. (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.answer: Work done = mgh = 100 × 10 × 10 = 10 000 J. Power = work / time = 10 000 / 20 = 500 W.
questions.explanation: Work against gravity divided by time gives the power.

questions.q: The relation between frequency f and time period T of a wave is
questions.explanation: Frequency is the reciprocal of the time period.

questions.q: The speed of sound in air at room temperature is about
questions.explanation: Sound travels at roughly 340 m/s in air.

questions.q: Sound is produced by
questions.explanation: Every sound comes from some vibration.

questions.q: The speed of sound in air increases when
questions.explanation: Sound travels faster in warmer air.

questions.q: Sound of frequency less than 20 Hz is called
questions.explanation: Infrasound lies below the audible range.

questions.q: A female voice is usually shriller than a male voice because its
questions.explanation: A higher frequency gives a higher pitch, which is heard as a shriller sound.

questions.q: State two uses of ultrasound.
questions.answer: Ultrasound is used to clean delicate parts such as electronic components, to detect flaws and cracks in metal blocks, and in ultrasonography to image organs inside the body.
questions.explanation: Ultrasound can reach places that are hard to reach and can reveal hidden structures.

questions.q: A person standing 25 m from a high wall claps his hands. Will he hear a distinct echo? Take the speed of sound as 344 m/s and the minimum time gap for a distinct echo as 0.1 s.
questions.answer: The sound travels 25 m to the wall and 25 m back, a total of 50 m. Time = 50 / 344 = about 0.145 s. This is more than 0.1 s, so he will hear a distinct echo.
keyPoints: Greater than 0.1 s so echo is heard
questions.explanation: An echo is heard separately if it arrives at least 0.1 s after the original sound.

questions.q: Separating the grain from the chaff using wind is called
questions.explanation: In winnowing, the lighter chaff is blown away by the wind.

questions.q: Cattle that are kept for milk production are called
questions.explanation: Milch animals are cows and buffaloes kept for milk.

questions.q: Fish obtained from the sea are caught from
questions.explanation: Marine fisheries are in sea water, while inland fisheries are in fresh water.

questions.q: Legumes improve soil fertility because bacteria in their root nodules
questions.explanation: Root nodule bacteria convert nitrogen of the air into usable compounds.

questions.q: Plants require 16 nutrients. How many of these are supplied by the soil?
questions.explanation: Air and water supply three of the nutrients; the soil supplies the other 13.

questions.q: An advantage of manure that chemical fertilisers do not have is that manure
options: has a high percentage of nutrients
adds humus and improves the structure of the soil
questions.explanation: Manure is rich in organic matter that improves soil structure and water retention.

questions.q: Name the two kinds of fisheries and give a difference between them.
questions.answer: The two kinds are marine fisheries and inland fisheries. Marine fisheries are in the sea and use sea water, while inland fisheries are in fresh water such as rivers, canals and ponds.
questions.explanation: Fish are obtained from both sea and fresh water.

questions.q: Why is bee-keeping useful to farmers apart from giving honey?
questions.answer: Bees visit flowers to collect nectar and pollen and in doing so they carry pollen from flower to flower, which helps pollination and increases crop yield. Beeswax is also obtained.
questions.explanation: Bee-keeping on a farm supports the production of crops that depend on pollination.
